run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-18T01:35:10Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on frontend-proxy is explained by gateway-level 504s: frontend-proxy's ingress server spans carry error=true with http.status_code 504 and a duration of ~15.0 s, i.e. Envoy's request timeout, throughout the visible window (first metric sample 01:36:10, alert start 01:35:10). Whole traces show the timed-out requests are POSTs to frontend's /api/checkout: frontend POST /api/checkout -> grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder -> checkout 'orders publish' which blocks ~78-89 s and fails with otel.status_description 'circuit breaker is open' before the proxy's 15 s timeout returns 504 to the load-generator. checkout's own logs show 'Failed to write message: kafka: Failed to produce message to topic orders: circuit breaker is open' from 01:34:49 (before the alert time) and 'read tcp 100.96.1.134:53048->100.71.78.255:9092: i/o timeout', where 100.71.78.255:9092 is the kafka Service ClusterIP. In namespace chaos-mesh, events show Schedule otel-demo-checkout-kafka-network-partition spawning NetworkChaos objects every minute (01:54:39-02:02:39), each reporting 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/checkout-5dccddf8bb-vn95l', 'otel-demo/kafka-ff7884766-xclnk' and 'otel-demo/kafka-ff7884766-skk8d', followed by TimeUp/Recovered; those are exactly the pods whose traffic is partitioned. A second, smaller error path also existed: frontend's grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds client spans errored between ~01:55 and 02:05 (median error duration ~1.1 ms, so not a 15 s timeout), and the ad pod was OOMKilled at 01:52:51; this is a separate, fast-failing fault whose contribution to the proxy's error count is unverified. Conclusion is partial because chaos events before 01:52:51 have expired and the alert rule itself is not available in this Prometheus, so the applier active at the 01:35:10 alert onset is inferred, not observed.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's error signal is on its ingress server span: 5-minute error-span increases for service_name=frontend-proxy, span_name='ingress' were 82.3 at 01:37, 118-145 through 01:53, peaked at 360 at 01:57-02:01 and were still 49.4 in the last partial step; the corresponding STATUS_CODE_UNSET stream stayed roughly flat at ~1,810-2,470 per 5 minutes, so the error rate, not the request volume, changed.

frontend-proxy has only two span operations, 'ingress' (span kind server) and 'router frontend egress' (span kind client); its error spans are http.status_code 504 with otel.status_code ERROR and durations of 15,001,066-15,001,929 us, i.e. a 15-second proxy timeout, not a fast rejection.

Trace f18dd56ad5afb108674a31c6c7770ed1 shows the exact hang path: load-generator POST 15.004 s with http.status_code 504 -> frontend-proxy 'ingress' 15.002 s http.status_code 504 -> frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress' 15.002 s error=true -> frontend 'POST /api/checkout' 89.085 s -> checkout 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' 89.082 s -> checkout 'orders publish' 88.872 s with error=true and otel.status_description 'circuit breaker is open'.

The same pattern was already present at 01:44:56 (still before the observed chaos events): three frontend-proxy 'ingress' spans with http.status_code 504 and 15.001 s duration, with checkout 'orders publish' spans of 78.688 s and 78.088 s carrying otel.status_description 'circuit breaker is open'.

checkout container logs record 'Failed to write message: kafka: Failed to produce message to topic orders: circuit breaker is open' at 01:35:56 and 'Failed to write message: circuit breaker is open' repeatedly (51 matching lines in 01:24-01:36, 298 in 01:25-01:45), and at 02:03:18 'client/metadata got error from broker 1 while fetching metadata: read tcp 100.96.1.134:53048->100.71.78.255:9092: i/o timeout'.
checkout's Kafka produce failures are visible at 01:34:49, i.e. about 21 seconds before the alert's 01:35:10 start, so the failing mechanism was already active when the alert fired.

The address checkout timed out to, 100.71.78.255:9092, is the 'kafka' Service ClusterIP and port in namespace otel-demo; the kafka pods themselves are kafka-ff7884766-skk8d at 100.96.2.21 and kafka-ff7884766-xclnk at 100.96.4.61, so the failure is at the service/connection level, not a single pod address.

Events in namespace chaos-mesh show that Schedule otel-demo-checkout-kafka-network-partition spawned a new NetworkChaos object every minute from 01:54:39 to 02:02:39, and each instance reported 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/checkout-5dccddf8bb-vn95l', 'otel-demo/kafka-ff7884766-xclnk' and 'otel-demo/kafka-ff7884766-skk8d', followed about 55 s later by TimeUp and 'Successfully recover chaos' for the same three pods.

Across the window the events group as 27 NetworkChaos 'Applied', 9 'Started', 8 'TimeUp', 24 'Recovered' and 102 'Updated' in namespace chaos-mesh, plus 51 'Updated' events on PodNetworkChaos objects in namespace otel-demo for checkout-5dccddf8bb-vn95l, kafka-ff7884766-skk8d and kafka-ff7884766-xclnk only; no chaos object is reported for frontend, frontend-proxy, ad or flagd pods.

checkout latency is dominated by that blocked publish: histogram_quantile(0.95) of traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket for checkout span_name='oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' is 15000 ms at every 2-minute step from 01:45 to 02:07, and the median duration of the errored 'orders publish' spans is likewise 15000 ms (top finite bucket), matching the 78-89 s spans seen in traces.

The errored 'orders publish' stream is continuous rather than bursty: its STATUS_CODE_ERROR increase per 5 minutes is 109.9, 146.7, 138.9 (and 118.5-123.3 earlier) between 01:45 and 02:05, consistent with a partition that is re-applied roughly every minute.

A second frontend error path exists but fails fast: frontend client spans grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds and frontend GET /api/data were STATUS_CODE_ERROR from the 01:55:00 bucket through 02:05:00 (up to 224.4 errored spans per 5 minutes), and the median duration of the errored GetAds spans is about 1.1 ms, not a 15 s timeout.

ad-554b849958-4chjq restarted at 01:52:51 after its container terminated with exitCode 137 and reason OOMKilled (restartCount 1, container ready now); the ad deployment sets a memory limit of 450Mi for that container.

The workloads involved are otherwise up: deployments frontend-proxy 1/1 ready/available, checkout 1/1, frontend 1/1, ad 1/1, kafka 2/2, with no unavailableReplicas, and the frontend-proxy and checkout pods have restartCount 0; chaos-mesh is therefore the only observed object applying a fault to the pods in the failing path.

Other backends showed no error spans in the same 10-minute reading: cart, currency, product-catalog, payment, shipping, quote, email, recommendation and image-provider had no STATUS_CODE_ERROR increase, while only frontend-proxy ingress (221.3), frontend GetAds/GET api/data (10.2), checkout 'orders publish' (141.9), ad flagd ResolveBoolean (38.9) and a few ~1-per-5-min flagd EventStream series were non-zero.

No traces_span_metrics samples exist in this Prometheus before about 01:36:10 (a query over 00:35:10-01:40:00 returned its first point at 01:36:10, and a 00:40-02:14 query reports source_start_at 01:37:00), so the frontend-proxy error rate cannot be compared with a pre-alert baseline.

The fault is a network partition between checkout and the kafka Service applied by the chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-checkout-kafka-network-partition: checkout can reach nothing at 100.71.78.255:9092 (i/o timeout), its producer circuit breaker opens, each publish blocks for ~78-89 s, frontend's /api/checkout exceeds the proxy's 15 s timeout and frontend-proxy answers 504 - which is what the RequestErrorRate alert counts.

The ad service OOMKill and its flagd ResolveBoolean client errors form a separate, second fault that probably contributed additional error responses at frontend-proxy between roughly 01:53 and 02:05, but it cannot explain the 15 s 504s because its errored GetAds spans last about 1.1 ms (fast failures).

A frontend-proxy or frontend application fault (crash, restart, bad image, unready replicas) was considered and rejected as the cause: frontend-proxy and checkout pods have restartCount 0, all deployments report 1/1 ready with no unavailable replicas, and the 504s carry parent-child spans into a healthy frontend whose 89 s child span ends in checkout, so the proxy is timing out waiting, not itself failing.

A kafka-side outage (brokers down or failing) was considered and left without support: both kafka pods are running with restartCount 0 and the kafka deployment reports 2/2 ready, kafka-ff7884766-xclnk logs continue normal broker work such as 'Sent auto-creation request for Set(__consumer_offsets)...' at 02:03:45, and the checkout error is a connection-level 'i/o timeout' to the kafka Service address rather than a broker error response.

Verify the Schedule otel-demo-checkout-kafka-network-partition (chaos-mesh) and its current NetworkChaos targets/duration in the chaos-mesh configuration, since its spec could not be read with the available resource kinds, and confirm whether the partition is meant to run this long.

Review the ad deployment's 450Mi memory limit together with the OOMKill of ad-554b849958-4chjq, and inspect the flagd reachability from ad (its flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean client spans error), as a second, independent error source.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule could not be read: list_prometheus_rules returned no_data both with rule_name=RequestErrorRate and with no filter, so the rule expression, threshold (annotation says above 0) and which status codes it counts are unverified.

Chaos evidence before 01:52:51 is missing because events only cover their own timestamps in the retained window (first otel-demo event 01:52:51, first chaos-mesh event 01:54:39); the NetworkChaos instance active at the 01:35:10 alert onset was therefore not observed, only inferred from checkout's failures at 01:34:49.

No traces_span_metrics samples exist before about 01:36:10 in this Prometheus, so no pre-alert baseline for the frontend-proxy error rate exists and the size of the deviation at alert time cannot be quantified.

The NetworkChaos and Schedule specs could not be read (their kinds are not among the queryable resources), so partition direction, selector, duration and whether the schedule is still active are unknown; only event messages and the observed consequences are evidence.
frontend pod logs could not be read (0 lines/0 bytes for frontend-675fd7b5c5-djtdf), so no application-side confirmation of the frontend's 89 s /api/checkout handling or of the GetAds errors exists.

The ad container's previous (pre-OOMKill) instance logs are unavailable and the current instance's logs contain no error/fail lines, so the reason for its failure beyond the OOMKilled record and its link to the flagd ResolveBoolean errors are unverified.

kube-state-metrics series are absent from this Prometheus (kube_deployment_status_replicas_available and all kube_* names returned no_data), so replica/readiness history during the window could not be checked, only the current object state.

No data on configuration or deployment change history is available (the change_history integration is not integrated), so whether the chaos schedule or the ad memory limit changed during the window is unknown.

Whether the fast-failing ad/GetAds errors actually produced error responses at frontend-proxy (and thus contributed to RequestErrorRate) was not verified; a search for frontend-proxy ingress spans with http.status_code 500 returned nothing, which is unknown rather than proof of absence.
The final 02:09-02:14 points are truncated/partial buckets, so the apparent recovery after the last observed chaos recovery at 02:02:34 is not confirmed.
next_steps: Inspect the Schedule otel-demo-checkout-kafka-network-partition and the NetworkChaos objects it creates in namespace chaos-mesh (targets, action, duration, direction) to confirm the partition window and whether it recurred from 01:35 onwards.
Retrieve the RequestErrorRate rule definition and confirm which span status codes and windows it aggregates.
Review the ad deployment memory limit (450Mi) and ad's connectivity to flagd to address the separate OOMKilled/flagd-resolution fault.
If the checkout-kafka partition is not intended, pause the chaos schedule and confirm checkout 'orders publish' latency and frontend-proxy 504s return to a pre-fault baseline.
